notes: Each requirement names the sections of docs/specs.md that state it (their anchors), the conformance vectors that exercise it (JSON pointers into kat/v0.3/vectors.json; '#id' selects the array element with that id), the reference-implementation tests that check it (nextest binary id and test path), and its origin: findings and proposals of the 2026-09-25 audit (C-, H-, M-, L-, P-) or decisions of the v0.3 design note (D-).

crates/cityg-core/tests/conformance_manifest.rs checks that every anchor, vector, test, script, model file and origin exists, that every normative section and every vector section is covered, and that every test of cityg-core is mapped to a requirement.
formal lists the ProVerif scenarios of docs/formal/ that state the requirement; docs/formal/run.sh checks their verdicts.
Sections listed in informative_sections state no requirement: informative text, or a heading whose subsections carry the requirements.

requirements.title: The protocol provides the properties of section 2.2 against the stated adversaries, and a deployment does not advertise more
The delivery service verifies commits against public state only and never holds a group secret
Signatures are FIPS 204 ML-DSA-65 with 32-byte seeds, hedged signing randomness from the caller, and the FIPS 204 sizes
Every signature uses the FIPS 204 context string of its usage; a signature does not verify under another context
Malformed signing keys, public keys and signatures are rejected before use

The KEM is X-Wing (draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-06): 32-byte decapsulation keys, 64 bytes of caller randomness per encapsulation, 1216-byte keys and 1120-byte ciphertexts, the FIPS 203 input check on every encapsulation key, and KeyGen from ExpandLabel
Objects are exchanged as deterministic CBOR (RFC 8949 section 4.2.1); decoders re-encode and reject any other encoding
H_L hashes the CBOR array [profile tag, label, args]; no map is ever an argument list
Extract, ExpandLabel, DeriveSecret, MAC and KeyGen are keyed BLAKE3 with the label, context and length bound into the input
Signed arrays carry their label and field count, which are checked before the signature over the rebuilt TBS
gid, device_id, invite_id, proposal_ref, epoch_ref and H_pk are the labelled hashes of section 5
The gid binds the creator's device key and nonce: a genesis is valid only if they hash to its gid
Members are named by their occupancy [leaf, since], which no later occupant of the leaf can take, even after the tree shrinks and grows again

The ratchet tree uses the RFC 9420 array layout; its capacity is a power of two between 2 and MAX_CAPACITY, its width is canonical, members enter the lowest blank leaf or the leaf the doubling tree adds, and a full group refuses joins

Leaves hold the member records, parents a key and their unmerged leaves; entering members are unmerged at their keyed ancestors, removals blank the leaf and its direct path, device keys are distinct, and snapshot decoders check every invariant
The tree hash binds every leaf by index and every parent's key and unmerged leaves, hashed apart from its children
The resolution of a node lists the node and its unmerged leaves, or the resolutions of its children when it is blank, in increasing node order

Every commit renews its author's leaf key from a fresh leaf secret and re-keys its direct path; path secrets are wrapped to the resolution of each copath node in the staged tree, and the commit secret is one derivation past the root
Update paths are validated without secrets: occupied author leaf, one entry per direct-path node, targets exactly the copath resolutions in order, valid keys and sizes
A receiver checks every derived node key against the published one; any decryption or key mismatch is a cover failure
An update path of a tree of capacity c fits max_update_path_bytes(c) and a commit fits max_commit_bytes(c)
A leaf proof carries the leaf, the width, the leaf node and one parent digest and sibling hash per level, is at most 8 KiB, and verifies only against the tree hash it was made for
The registry hash covers the capacity, the admin leaves in increasing order, the retired admissions and the retired floor; decoders check the registry's invariants
Admins are named by their leaf, at most MAX_ADMINS; their rights end with their occupancy, survive a resync and a rotation, and the author of a commit that leaves no admin becomes one
The admission of a removed member is retired while it could be used, and the retired floor refuses it once its entry is dropped: a removed member cannot come back with an admission it kept
GroupContext_n binds gid, epoch, tree hash, registry hash, profile and confirmed transcript hash into every epoch secret
Epoch secrets chain through init_secret: the joiner secret, then the epoch, init, msg, confirm and external secrets derive as in section 8
Confirmed and interim transcript hashes chain every commit, including its rotation signature; the confirmation tag authenticates the confirmed transcript
Members erase the secrets of an epoch when the next one becomes active, keeping only its init and external secrets until then
External init: the epoch's external X-Wing key derives from external_secret, and a joiner's or resyncing member's encapsulation yields the init secret members recover
A commit is a CBOR map with a closed key registry; unknown, missing or forbidden keys make it malformed
Every commit carries one ML-DSA-65 signature by its author over the map without keys 109 to 111, and a second one by the new key exactly when it rotates the author's key
A genesis is the epoch-0 commit of its creator: leaf 0 since epoch 0, sole admin, ZERO32 initial secrets

Transition order: pruning, authorized removals (never of the author), admin changes by an admin, entries at the entry leaf with admissions authorized against the admins at that point, rotation, promotion, truncation, then the update path
The resulting tree hash and registry hash must equal those the commit announces

Verifiers check gid, epoch and the previous interim transcript hash, so commits of another group or a forked history are rejected, and no secret of an epoch is used before its confirmation tag verified
A member that lost its state or could not process a commit re-enters its own leaf as a new occupancy with a Resync commit through the external init
An ExternalJoin puts its author at the entry leaf first and may carry the other recorded removals and join requests, whose joiners enter with welcomes
A removal proposal is signed by its target (leave) or by an admin, names a current occupancy, and is single use
A member never commits its own removal: another member commits it, or a joiner
Post-removal secrecy: the removed leaf and its direct path are blanked in the tree the removing commit encrypts to, so the removed member derives no later epoch secret
Invites are signed by an admin with an expiry and a use count; the invite key derives from a 32-byte invite seed and names the invite

Admissions are signed by an admin (kind 0) or by an invite key whose invite an admin signed (kind 1), name the device and a last epoch within MAX_ADMISSION_EPOCHS, and are authorized against the admins of the epoch the join enters
The tree records each member's admission hash, so the delivery service cannot add a member on its own
Invite revocations are signed by an admin; the delivery service refuses revoked and used-up invites and drops the recorded requests that rely on a revoked one

A join request is signed by the joining device and carries its leaf key, a one-time init key and its admission; it is authorized for an epoch when the device is not a member and its admission is authorized

The author of a commit seals one welcome per included request, in order, to the request's init key, under a context binding gid, epoch, request_ref and the key; it carries the joiner secret of the epoch

A joiner enters with its welcome only after checking that the commit includes its request unchanged, the confirmation tag and the GroupInfo, then decrypts the update path with its leaf key and erases its init key; it learns nothing of earlier epochs
The GroupInfo of an epoch is signed by the commit author for its leaf and verified against the tree and registry whose hashes it binds
A member that cannot process a commit signs a cover-failure report, which the delivery service records for current members and the current epoch, then resyncs

A Member commit may rotate its author's device key: the new key is no member's, signs the commit under its own context, and takes over the occupancy, admission and admin rights, while messages of earlier epochs verify under the key held then
Messages are FramedContent signed under city-g/msg/v4 and sealed in an envelope whose header (epoch_ref, sender occupancy, generation, key commitment) is the AEAD associated data
Each member sends on its own chain, keyed by its occupancy, with strictly increasing generations derived from msg_secret; keys are erased once used

Receivers accept a message only from the same occupancy in its epoch and in the current one, without a recorded removal, within the generation bounds, and verify its signature under the key the sender held in that epoch
Messages of up to MAX_GRACE_EPOCHS previous epochs stay readable for GRACE_WINDOW_MS after the next epoch began, then their keys are erased
The ledger starts from a valid genesis and accepts the first valid commit of each epoch; a later commit for the same epoch is rejected
Removal proposals and join requests are recorded once, if authorized; every commit includes the oldest overdue ones up to the caps, and the others are authorized again after each commit
The delivery service stores the welcomes of each commit by request reference and answers each request's status
The ledger stores admin-signed invites (at most MAX_INVITES), counts their uses and refuses expired, revoked or used-up invites and the joins that embed them
The ledger relays an envelope once per (epoch, sender, generation), for the current epoch or one of the grace epochs, only from a current member of both epochs without a recorded removal
The log numbers entries from 1, expires messages before commits, and bounds its size without dropping the entry it appends or the latest commit
The delivery service journals every change before answering and rebuilds a group deterministically from its snapshot and records

The delivery service keeps the LightCommit of each accepted commit, computed from the tree the commit starts from, serves leaf proofs against the current tree, and the LightJoin of a committed request while its epoch is current
Members create groups, sign admissions with invite links, record join requests, wait for a commit to include them and otherwise commit their own entry
Members follow the log in order, recognize their own commits, resync after a failure or a lost commit, and delete the group state when removed
Members persist their state after encrypting and before sending, after every commit and after following the log, protected at rest
Members commit the recorded proposals of others, re-key their leaf at least every FS_WINDOW, and stop committing and sending once their own removal is recorded
A light member keeps the context, registry, occupancies, its own record and private path, and at most MAX_KNOWN_KEYS verified device keys; it becomes full with a snapshot that matches its state

A light member processes a commit in the order of section 14.2: checks without the tree, proofs against the previous tree hash, the transition on its partial tree, the path shape, the registry hash, the path secret and the confirmation tag
A LightCommit holds the leaf proofs, against the previous tree, of every member record the commit's authorization refers to, by increasing leaf
A light joiner checks the registry, its leaf proof and the occupancies of its LightJoin against the commit before decrypting the update path
Messages from senders a light member does not know wait for a leaf proof; light members do not author commits and become full to commit

A light member verifies every signature, authorization, entry leaf, the registry, path secrets and the confirmation tag, and relies on the delivery service only for the new tree hash and device-key uniqueness
Aliases are self-asserted signed bindings with validated display names; clients pin the occupancy first seen for an alias
A fresh SessionAuth signed by a current member is exchanged for a bearer token that stops working when the occupancy ends or the key is rotated
The /v3 HTTP API carries protobuf requests whose field 1 is the gid and protocol objects as their exact bytes, maps errors to the statuses of section 15.2, and answers 410 on /v1 and /v2
The WebSocket notifies log heads and asks clients to fetch the log after dropped notices
Invite links use version 5 and carry the DS URL, gid and invite seed; other versions are refused
Protocol parameters and delivery-service defaults follow section 16 and are validated at configuration time
Every labelled hash, derivation label, framing tag and object label is the one registered in section 17
Every signed object uses the signature context registered for it in section 17.3
